subject: gov.policy
name: Broadband technical feasibility and security risk consultancy
milestone: Consultancy launched 25 October 2025
position_end: Launched, mapping existing broadband infrastructure and designing backbone and cross-border routes

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Inclusion Policy for marginalised groups
milestone: Validated at a stakeholder workshop
position_end: A national policy on access to ICT services for marginalised groups, finalised after a stakeholders' validation workshop

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030
milestone: Finalisation under way with ITU support, October 2025
position_start: A strategy in drafting with no finalisation process on record (2025-08)
position_end: Finalisation under way with ITU support; no adopted text, costing or delivery schedule published (2026-08)

subject: gov.policy
name: e-Government Strategy and Implementation Roadmap 2025-2029
milestone: Published August 2025
position_end: Published, stating that the federal government lacks an enterprise architecture and interoperability framework, and setting out a data-exchange hub, a national enterprise service bus and shared services as the corrective

subject: gov.policy
name: National Communications Authority strategic plan
status: In development, draft put to public comment
milestone: Public comments open to 20 July 2023
position_end: The regulator's first strategic plan, of eight objectives and 14 initiatives, was put out for public comment until 20 July 2023; no adopted version is on the repository

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Policy Framework
milestone: Validated, reported 2026-03-13
position_end: A framework for how data is collected, managed, shared and protected, with interoperability, classification and retention standards and a data-sovereignty aim; validated, with adoption not on record
note: a development agency's account; the text and any adoption are not held

subject: gov.policy
name: National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024
milestone: Adopted by Cabinet; covered 2019 to 2024
position_end: Expired, having documented five mobile operators employing about 25,000 people and mobile money running at 150 million transactions a month

subject: gov.policy
name: National ICT Policy and Strategy 2025-2029
milestone: Drafting consultancy called, expressions of interest due 29 November 2025
position_end: A four-month consultancy to renew the expired 2019-2024 policy for 2025-2029 was called under the regional digital integration project, with expressions of interest due 29 November 2025
note: the minister told a United Nations forum in July 2025 that a national ICT policy had been approved earlier that year; the November call to draft one is the later record

subject: gov.policy
name: Somali Customs Strategic Plan 2024-2027
milestone: Plan period opened 2024
position_end: Five objectives for federal and member-state customs, including full rollout of the SOMCAS automated customs system planned for 2024

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybersecurity Law
status: In development, passed by the lower house and at first reading in the upper
milestone: First reading in the Upper House, 29 August 2026
position_start: A Cybercrimes Bill developed by the communications ministry given its first reading in the House of the People on 8 December 2025 without substantive debate and referred to committee for a second, and a cybersecurity law approved by the House of the People on 26 January 2026 assigning policy to the communications ministry, technical oversight to the regulator and obligations to critical-infrastructure operators
position_end: A six-chapter, 33-article bill given its first reading in the Upper House on 29 August 2026, at the first sitting of its eighth term, short of the second and third readings the chamber requires for final approval
note: the repository carries three differently named stages — a Cybercrimes Bill at first reading in the lower house, a cybersecurity law approved by that house, and a bill at first reading in the upper house — and does not state that they are one instrument; the chamber’s own published procedure is the source for the three readings it requires

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Transactions Bill
status: In development, passed by the House of the People
milestone: Approved by the House of the People with 137 votes, 2026-10-21
position_end: Drafted by the communications ministry to set a legal framework for digital transactions and mobile money, and approved by the House of the People with 137 votes in favour; the Senate stage and assent are not on record
note: the ministry's own release; the bill text is not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Draft Penal Code replacing the 1962 code
milestone: Under review in the House of the People, 2026-10-14
position_end: A draft code before Parliament to replace the 1962 Penal Code, with provisions for offences involving digital platforms and information systems; no timetable for a final vote

subject: gov.legislate
name: Mobile Money Regulations 2020
milestone: Amended 2020 under the Central Bank Act 2012
position_end: In force, covering licensing, conduct of business, safeguarding of consumer funds, supervision and winding-up of mobile money providers

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Communications Law 2017
milestone: The regulator's type-approval guidelines issued under it July 2020
position_start: a Communications Bill through two of its three parliamentary readings (January 2017)
position_end: in force: the regulator issued its July 2020 type-approval guidelines under Article 59 of the Communications Act 2017

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payment System Bill
milestone: Third reading passed 28-0 in the Upper House, 11 January 2026
position_end: Through both chambers — 154 to 2 in the lower house and 28 to nil in the upper — creating a unified framework for the central bank to license and supervise payment systems and digital-money platforms

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Statistics Law (Law 24 of 2020)
milestone: Assented 24 February 2020, repealing the 1970 statistics law
position_end: In force, establishing the national statistics bureau in place of the 1970 law
note: The statute's own text was not located; the bureau's institutional statement stands in

subject: gov.legislate
name: Official Information Bill
milestone: Before the House of the People since March 2024; passed by Cabinet, awaiting ratification
position_start: Before the House of the People since March 2024
position_end: Still before the House of the People after eighteen months, criticised in an international review for broad national-security exemptions and no independent oversight
note: The constitution has directed Parliament to enact an implementing law since 2012

subject: gov.legislate
name: Population Registration and Civil Status Statistics Law (Law 46 of 2026)
milestone: Published in the Official Bulletin 5 April 2026
position_end: In force, establishing the civil-registration and vital-statistics layer beside the national identity infrastructure

subject: gov.legislate
name: Public Identification and Registration Law (Law 009 of 2023)
milestone: Implementing regulation made 8 June 2024
position_start: The Act alone, with no implementing regulation
position_end: In force with its implementing regulation, founding the identity authority and the national digital identity system

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulation on the Digitalisation of Public Financial Management 2025
milestone: Published in the Official Bulletin 2025-08-17
position_end: A finance ministry regulation under the 2019 public financial management Act covering electronic signatures, electronic records, fiscal data governance, continuity of the financial management system and the use of artificial intelligence

subject: gov.legislate
name: Telecommunications Consumer Protection Regulations
milestone: Formal 45-day public consultation opened 8 July 2026
position_end: Published for public comment to 31 August 2026 under the National Communications Law, covering pricing and contract transparency, service quality, operator obligations and enforcement

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Act (Law 005/2023)
milestone: In effect since 23 March 2023, with implementing regulations reviewed
position_start: In force, with lawful bases, data-subject rights and fines of 2-4% of worldwide turnover (2025-08)
position_end: In force and unamended; the Act does not define public data, which clouds the regulator's mandate (2026-08)
sources: 2024-06-11 Review of Somalia's Data Protection Act and implementing regulations|2023-03-22-somalia-data-protection-act-law-005-2023

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Authority
milestone: First nationwide enforcement step: mandatory registration under Article 32, June 2026
position_start: Inaugurated February 2024 and issuing guidelines, with no enforcement action on record (2025-08)
position_end: Requiring all controllers and processors to register and issuing compliance certificates; no penalty issued on record (2026-06)
sources: 2026-06-02-somalia-dpa-enforces-data-compliance-registration|2024-02-26 Somalia inaugurates its Data Protection Authority
note: Its independence is qualified by executive appointment and override powers.

subject: gov.protect
name: Regulatory framework for the public data protection law
milestone: Approved by the Council of Ministers on 8 January 2026 and adopted the following month
position_end: Adopted, operationalising the Act and aligning it to the digital transformation agenda (2026-02)

subject: gov.protect
name: Request to delay WhatsApp usernames
milestone: Request made in a regulator statement of 6 July 2026 and restated by the minister on 22 July
position_end: Request outstanding with no platform response on record; Somalia is the second country after India to ask for a pause (2026-07)
note: The stated grounds are impersonation risk against the mobile-money system and loss of phone-number traceability in the campaign against al-Shabab.

subject: gov.regional
name: Accession to the African Continental Free Trade Area
milestone: Instrument of ratification to be deposited September 2026
position_end: Somalia is to become the 50th state party on depositing its instrument of ratification in September 2026, having agreed with the Secretariat at Mogadishu on 18 August 2026 a sequence running from ratification through domesticating the electronic tariff book and configuring preferential tariffs in the customs administration to completing outstanding East African Community tariff and services commitments and a first shipment, with the continental payment system and the AfCFTA Adjustment Fund named as the instruments available and the national chamber of commerce asking for access to services markets including telecommunications, logistics, finance and digital commerce
note: the Secretariat's own release; its standfirst dates the deposit to 2 September 2026 while its body says only September, and the wider month is what is carried here

subject: gov.regional
name: Accession to the East African One Network Area
milestone: Operator consultation on the national roadmap, 18 September 2025
position_end: A national roadmap under consultation with licensed operators, setting phased alignment of national law and tariffs with the regional roaming framework

subject: gov.regional
name: Connection to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System
status: In development, membership signed, connection targeted for end-2026
milestone: Membership agreement signed March 2026; connection targeted before end-2026
position_end: The central bank signed the membership agreement in March 2026 and is onboarding, a June 2026 workshop briefing commercial banks, with the national payment switch's connection stated as a target for before the end of 2026

subject: gov.regional
name: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project financing agreement
milestone: Signed 21 June 2023
position_end: A binding grant agreement of SDR 59.5 million establishing participation in cross-border terrestrial links, national backbone, regional exchange-point support and coordinated spectrum and cybersecurity platforms

subject: gov.regional
name: Peer-learning cooperation with Pakistan on digital identity and public infrastructure
milestone: Roundtable closed with an action matrix, Islamabad, 16 September 2026
position_end: A ten-day mission by a 15-member delegation closed with a roundtable that set three working groups (foundational identity; governance, interoperability and data exchange; financial inclusion and public financing) and an action matrix naming priority areas, focal points and 30-, 60- and 90-day steps
note: peer learning rather than a transfer of systems; no agreement or memorandum is published

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional harmonisation of cybersecurity legal frameworks
milestone: Terms of reference issued May 2024
position_end: A commissioned comparative study and recommendations to harmonise cybersecurity, cybercrime, data protection, digital identity and e-commerce law across member states

subject: gov.regional
name: Study of Tanzania's digital government systems
milestone: Delegation sent 2026-08-28
position_end: a government delegation studying labour and employment digital systems in Dodoma, and a stated intent to learn from the wider public-service digitalisation model

subject: gov.standards
name: Government information-systems audit cooperation programme
milestone: Third phase of the supreme-audit-institution programme completed, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a completed phase
position_end: The auditor general’s office and a partner supreme audit institution have completed the third phase of a cooperation programme on auditing government information systems; no audit report, scope or next phase date is on file

subject: gov.standards
name: Membership of the international standards organisation
milestone: Member body, with participating and observing status on technical committees
position_end: The national bureau of standards is the country's member body, holding participating and observing status on technical committees and observing status on a policy committee

subject: gov.standards
name: National Cybersecurity Compliance Framework
milestone: Published alongside the risk-management framework, 19 July 2026
position_end: Published with download links by the regulator, alongside the risk-management framework reported as aligned to the international information-security standards

subject: gov.standards
name: Type approval for radio and telecommunications terminal equipment
milestone: Issued July 2020 under the Communications Act 2017
position_end: Mandatory regulator approval before terminal equipment is marketed or used, tested against recognised European and international standards

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public argument on resource governance
milestone: Opinion published by a former prime minister
position_end: A published opinion by a former prime minister arguing the country cannot afford another term of lost wealth
note: a signed opinion rather than a policy position; it is held because public argument of this kind is otherwise absent from this ledger

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public debate on digital policy
milestone: Civil-society advocacy position issued 21 July 2026
position_end: A government-convened multi-stakeholder review of the draft cybersecurity framework in April 2026, and a civil-society advocacy position in July calling for ratification of the African Union data convention
note: Published civil-society analysis, a parliamentary debate record, or a consultation response on a digital instrument.

subject: gov.discourse
name: State takedown of social media pages
milestone: 82,000 pages closed in 2026, on the ministry’s own count
position_start: Thousands of pages closed across platforms in recent years, on the same ministry’s account, with no annual figure given
position_end: The information ministry’s director general said on 3 September 2026 that the federal government had closed 82,000 social media pages during 2026 that it alleges carried armed-group propaganda, across Facebook, TikTok and Telegram, and that the figure would keep rising because the year had not ended; he described the removals as the ideological front of a three-part counter-terrorism strategy alongside the military and economic ones (2026-09)
note: the count, the platforms and the attribution are the ministry’s own; no appeal route, oversight mechanism, legal basis or platform confirmation is stated

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic budget appropriations for the digital sector
milestone: 2026 Appropriation Act approved by a joint sitting of Parliament, 23 December 2025
movement: Advanced, the data protection authority's recurrent vote up by half
position_start: The 2025 Appropriation Act carries votes by budget head, among them the Data Protection Authority at US$162,060 recurrent and US$1,826,000 project (2025-01)
position_end: The 2026 Appropriation Act sets the Data Protection Authority's recurrent vote at US$242,540, above the US$170,880 the bill proposed; the budget framework still finances e-government, digital signatures and payments infrastructure from the general Government Local Fund rather than a dedicated digital line (2026-04)
note: the acts' schedules carry every federal vote, the telecommunications regulator among them as its own head; only the data protection authority's figures are stated in the record held

subject: finance.mou
name: Cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia on AI and space regulation
milestone: Signed in Riyadh at the global regulators' symposium
position_end: An agreement to develop a framework for cooperation on regulating artificial intelligence and space technology, covering regulatory cooperation, expertise sharing and infrastructure sharing
note: No primary announcement from either regulator was located; the record is a screened news report

subject: finance.mou
name: Framework cooperation agreement with the ITU
milestone: Signed in Manama, 7 November 2023
position_end: A framework agreement covering communication development, digital policy and regulation, digital skills, connectivity infrastructure and trust in digital services

subject: finance.mou
name: Memorandum with Türkiye's communications regulator
milestone: Signed in Ankara, 10 February 2026
position_end: A bilateral memorandum covering satellite-communications regulation, cybersecurity, spectrum management, broadband deployment, network resilience and regulatory capacity building

subject: finance.new
name: Blended financing facility for a microfinance institution
milestone: USD 3 million facility organised with two co-lenders
position_end: A USD 3 million Sharia-compliant facility for a Somali microfinance institution, the clearest private-capital mobilisation in the window into the financial services that carry mobile money

subject: finance.new
name: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project, Somalia component
milestone: Seventh implementation report; a mid-term review held January to April 2026 raised the development-objective rating from Moderately Unsatisfactory to Moderately Satisfactory
position_end: US$162m IDA across the project after a US$10m partial cancellation in Somalia in April 2026; implementation progress raised to Moderately Unsatisfactory and overall risk from High to Substantial, with fiduciary and environmental-and-social risk both still High (2026-06-16)
note: Private-sector investment mobilised in Somalia stands at US$0 against a US$10m target

subject: finance.new
name: Private capital mobilisation in the regional digital project

position_end: USD 30 million of unguaranteed commercial financing designed into a USD 172 million grant operation to draw private investment into backbone, backhaul and access networks

subject: finance.new
name: Smartphone financing programme
milestone: Launched May 2026, targeting 100,000 devices by end-2026
position_end: A private, Sharia-compliant device-finance scheme at USD 19 down and from USD 0.60 a day through a mobile-money platform, with 10,000 devices distributed initially and 100,000 targeted by the end of 2026

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank financing for the digital identity rollout
milestone: Officials put the remaining cost of completing the rollout at about US$125m, January 2026
position_start: SCALED-UP funding the identity toolset at US$75m (2025-08)
position_end: Identity a pillar of the SPRING initiative of more than US$100m, with about US$125m more estimated to complete the rollout and no funding source named (2026-01)
sources: 2025-12-17 Somalia digital ID major pillar of World Bank-funded SPRING initiative|2026-01-12 Somalia estimates $125 million needed to complete national digital ID rollout

subject: infra.connect
name: Berbera international gateway route
milestone: Positioned as an alternative regional gateway
position_end: The port city of Berbera is being positioned as an alternative digital gateway for landlocked neighbours, offering internet providers, businesses and governments another route to global data connections and cloud services beside the established Mombasa gateway. Capacity, operators and landing arrangements are not held
note: the account held is a free lede; the body sits behind a paywall, so only the claim is on file

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet use and price
milestone: Price position reported 2026-08-29
position_end: mobile data prices reported among the cheapest in Africa, alongside smartphone financing
note: Somalia ranks 191st on online government services in the same account.

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile connections
milestone: Measured at the end of 2025
position_start: 10.7 million connections at the end of 2024
position_end: 11.5 million active cellular connections at the end of 2025, 58.1 per cent of a 19.8 million population, of which 75.7 per cent broadband; up 757,000 or 7.0 per cent year on year

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile data price
milestone: Measured for 2024 on the regulator's price basket
position_start: USD 5.75 average mobile data cost in 2023
position_end: USD 5.10 average mobile data cost in 2024, down 11.3 per cent, with one gigabyte of residential mobile broadband around USD 5.65 at purchasing-power parity

subject: infra.connect
name: National interconnection between operators
milestone: Implemented across six licensed operators under a 2023 agreement, on the regulator's account
position_end: Voice calls interconnect across six licensed operators under a 2023 national agreement, on the regulator's account; mobile-money wallets remain closed to one another, and a smaller operator's chief executive says the dominant operators have little commercial incentive to open them
note: the account of the wallets is one operator's chief executive's, given in an interview

subject: infra.connect
name: Somali internet exchange point
milestone: Registry record last updated 28 September 2019
position_end: Registered to the communications regulator with address blocks allocated, and recording zero peers, zero connections and no IPv6 participation on its own entry

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite service
milestone: Available nationwide from August 2025, four months after licensing
position_start: Licensed in April 2025 after about two and a half years of talks, not yet available nationwide (2025-08)
position_end: Available across the country at US$390 for hardware and US$70 a month, US$210 for the mini terminal, with a first local reseller from September 2025 (2025-09)
note: Licensed on a full foreign-ownership model without major public debate, which is the fastest such accommodation on the wiki's West and East African record.

subject: infra.connect
name: Submarine cable landings and their regulatory framework
milestone: First submarine cable landing technical working group opened with the IFC, June 2026
position_start: Landings at Mogadishu, Berbera and Bosaso with no submarine cable regulatory framework on record (2025-08)
position_end: Working group opened on outage management, competition and a regulatory framework; no framework published (2026-06)

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial colocation data centres (Dalkom)
milestone: Offered as a standing service from two data centres
position_end: a telecom provider offering colocation in its own data centres in Mogadishu and Nairobi on a 10 Gbps backbone
note: no capacity, tenancy or customer figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial off-site backup and disaster recovery
milestone: Offered as a standing service from two locations
position_end: A national infrastructure provider advertising offshore backup in Mombasa and Mogadishu with real-time replication, continuous data protection and business-continuity planning
note: No capacity figure is published, and no government off-site arrangement is held

subject: infra.store
name: Golis Birta Dheer data centre, Garowe
milestone: Grounding and earthing installation under way
position_end: Under active construction near Garowe as a commercial operator facility in Puntland, distinct from the existing operator estate and the two government projects
note: Documented by an employee's own account rather than a corporate release

subject: infra.store
name: Government data-hosting and cloud guidelines
milestone: Still at its November 2022 baseline against an April 2028 target
position_end: None published (2026-06-16)
note: A results indicator of the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project; the World Bank records it as not achieved

subject: infra.store
name: Hormuud data centre estate
milestone: Operator stated to be investing in further local data centres and solar-powered network sites
position_start: 11 data centres of about 10 MWh, the working private hosting base (2024-12)
position_end: Further domestic capacity stated as under investment; no updated site count or load figure published (2026-06)
sources: 2024-12-09 Hormuud Telecom plans to build more green data centres|2026-06-18-hormuud-anchors-somalia-digital-economy

subject: infra.store
name: National Data Centre, Mogadishu
milestone: Restated as planned by the state minister for communications, 2026-08-07
position_start: Under construction and described as nearing completion, not launched (2025-05)
position_end: No launch recorded in the repository; on 7 August 2026 the state minister for communications described a National Data Centre as being planned to strengthen digital infrastructure, speaking at the launch of an artificial-intelligence product by a private centre
note: the ministry's stated rationale - to end reliance on data storage outside the country - is also its statement that government data was held offshore when it spoke. A facility described as nearing completion in May 2025 is described as planned fifteen months later, and the record does not reconcile the two

subject: infra.store
name: Open Access Data Centres facility, Mogadishu
status: Planned, end-2022 target passed with nothing on record
milestone: Expected in operation by the end of 2022, stated November 2021
position_end: A carrier-neutral data centre at the Mogadishu submarine cable landing, in the first phase of a pan-African network funded from a US$124m equity raise and US$200m in total capital by its wholesale-carrier parent, expected to be operational by the end of 2022
note: the financial adviser's own announcement; no construction, opening or capacity record for the Mogadishu site is held

subject: infra.store
name: Somaliland government data centre
milestone: Groundbreaking 22 September 2025 in Hargeisa
position_end: Under construction as Somaliland's first government data centre and cybersecurity management centre, with external technical-mission support

subject: infra.energy
name: Bosaso power grid rehabilitation
milestone: Appraisal report dated November 2025
position_end: Appraised at UA 18.021 million to rehabilitate and expand the Bosaso grid and strengthen energy-sector institutions, executed federally with Puntland as implementing agency

subject: infra.energy
name: National electricity licensing and tariff framework
milestone: 20 providers licensed at a consultation on 1 and 2 November 2025
position_end: The first unified, legally recognised licensing system since 1991: 20 electricity service providers licensed and a national tariff regulation framework validated under the Electricity Act 2023

subject: infra.energy
name: National electricity system
milestone: Assessed June 2025 and endorsed 8 July 2025
position_end: Isolated island networks with no national transmission grid, several vertically integrated private suppliers per city, generation dominated by high-speed diesel, and distribution losses reported up to 50 per cent

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural electricity access
milestone: No national rural access figure published; first official SDG 7 energy indicators report issued January 2026
position_end: No rural electricity access figure is published in the held record; the country's first official SDG 7 energy indicators report was issued in January 2026, drawing on energy ministry, national electricity authority and World Bank data
note: the report's data analysis chapter, which carries the rural access figures, would settle it

subject: infra.energy
name: Somali Electricity Sector Recovery Project
milestone: 150 public health facilities connected, inaugurated 1 October 2025
position_start: No public facilities solarised under the project
position_end: 150 public health facilities connected to solar with battery storage and 215 educational facilities to follow, solar installation begun in three cities, and 6,113,047 people recorded as cumulatively reached

subject: infra.energy
name: Transformational Access and Infrastructure Resilience Programme
milestone: Concept-stage document prepared 7 February 2026
position_end: A USD 100 million grant at concept stage whose first pillar includes reliable power and water supply at Mogadishu and four regional airport facilities

subject: infra.capacity
name: National IPv6 migration
milestone: Migration accelerated by the regulator and a National IPv6 Centre
position_start: Strategy adopted February 2025, with no migration activity on record (2025-08)
position_end: Migration running with a National IPv6 Centre at Jamhuriya University; no adoption percentage published (2026-06)

subject: infra.capacity
name: Telecom Regulatory Management Information System
milestone: Reported in the regulator's 2024/2025 annual report
position_end: The regulator's own operating systems — a market observatory framework and a regulatory management information system — reported as in service

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Risk Management Framework
milestone: Launched 21 July 2026, after a national consultation in April
position_end: Launched covering risk identification, regulatory compliance and institutional responsibilities; no compliance deadline or reporting duty published (2026-07)

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Somalia Computer Incident Response Team (SOMCIRT)
milestone: Opened by the Prime Minister, 7 March 2026
position_start: Did not exist; provided for in the Cybersecurity Law (2025-08)
position_end: Operating to coordinate prevention, detection and response and to issue national cybersecurity alerts (2026-03)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Caafimaad+ digitalised data system
milestone: Scaled from five facilities to over 40 across nine regions
position_end: Over 40 facilities across nine regions and more than 25 districts, pushing frontline clinical data into the federal health platform in real time

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Government API gateway, single sign-on and national digital government portal
milestone: Design-and-deploy consultancy tendered 16 October 2026
position_end: The communications ministry invited firms to design, deploy and operate a production API gateway, government single sign-on and a national portal under the regional digital integration project, building on an enterprise architecture and interoperability framework from an earlier package; expressions of interest due 29 October 2026

subject: dpi.exchange
name: High School Certificate system
milestone: Connects identity, payments and registry building blocks
position_end: Connecting registration, identity verification and consent, payments and the examination registry so results are retrieved automatically and certificates issued digitally

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Interoperability between government systems
milestone: Named as the central risk in a domestic analysis and in the DPI summit communique, April 2026
position_start: No national coordination forum on record (2025-08)
position_end: First national DPI summit held in February 2026 with the Central Bank, the regulator, the identity authority and the data protection authority; no interoperability standard or role-clarity instrument published (2026-04)
